name: IntelliPOS E-commerce Fiscalization
author: obelusdoo

sections.description:
IntelliPOS E-commerce Fiscalization connects a WooCommerce store in Serbia to the merchant’s IntelliPOS instance. When an order reaches the status you choose, the plugin sends it to IntelliPOS, which issues the fiscal receipt through the Tax Administration fiscal processor (PFR). The receipt number, receipt time and journal are stored with the order.

The plugin is free, but fiscalization is not. The plugin is not an ESIR and cannot issue fiscal receipts on its own: every receipt is issued by your IntelliPOS instance, which requires an active paid IntelliPOS license and a security element. Installing the plugin alone does not let you fiscalize orders.

Pricing

  • IntelliPOS E-commerce Fiscalization (this plugin): free, no additional fee.
  • IntelliPOS annual license without advance invoices: RSD 14,388 + VAT per year.
  • IntelliPOS annual license with advance invoices: RSD 18,000 + VAT per year.

Prices as of October 2026. Request a license at intellipos.rs.

What it does

  • Issues a fiscal receipt automatically when an order reaches a selected status (for example “Processing”), or manually from the order screen.
  • Training mode for testing: with the invoice type set to “Obuka”, IntelliPOS issues training receipts that are not fiscal receipts and are not recorded as turnover. Switch back to “Promet” when the store goes live.
  • Runs in the background, so customers do not wait for the fiscal processor at checkout.
  • Shows the receipt on the order: status, fiscal number, document number, receipt time, journal and a link to the Tax Administration verification page.
  • Issues a full fiscal refund manually, or automatically when an order is fully refunded in WooCommerce. Before every full refund it checks in IntelliPOS that no part of the receipt was refunded already.
  • Optional (off by default, requires a newer IntelliPOS server): issues a fiscal partial refund for each WooCommerce refund by items, quantity, item amount, shipping or fees.
  • Optionally asks IntelliPOS to e-mail the fiscal receipt to the customer. The order shows that IntelliPOS accepted the request; delivery is not confirmed.
  • Adds customer type, company name and tax ID (PIB, 9 digits) fields to the classic checkout and to the Checkout block.
  • Maps WooCommerce tax classes to IntelliPOS tax labels and checks that each item’s VAT rate matches its label.
  • Maps each payment method to the payment type printed on the receipt.
  • Sends products, shipping and fees as receipt items and checks that the receipt total equals the amount paid.
  • Supports High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS); pauses fiscalization on a copy of the site (staging) until an administrator confirms it.

Built for unclear outcomes

Networks fail. When the plugin cannot be sure whether a receipt was issued (a timeout, a broken connection or a server error after sending), it does not send the order again. The order is marked “unknown outcome” and the administrator follows a guided check in IntelliPOS: link the existing receipt, or confirm that none was issued and only then send it again. Every decision is logged.

  • One fiscalization request per order and at most one request per refund, each with a fixed external ID.
  • Repeated clicks, repeated status changes and repeated payment notifications do not send a second request.
  • Automatic triggers send only the first attempt; nothing is retried on its own after an error.

Limitation: the IntelliPOS service does not currently reject a second request with the same external ID. The plugin therefore cannot guarantee by itself that a duplicate receipt is impossible; an incorrect manual confirmation on the resolution page can still produce one.

What the plugin does not do

  • With partial refunds off (the default), or with an older IntelliPOS server, partial refunds are recorded in order notes but not sent. Refunds entered as an amount only, without items, are never sent automatically.
  • Orders in a currency other than RSD and orders with negative fees are not fiscalized; the order note explains why.
  • Receipt e-mail delivery is not confirmed. IntelliPOS reports only that it accepted the send request; whether the message arrives depends on the mail setup of the IntelliPOS server.
  • The plugin transfers order data to your IntelliPOS instance. The merchant remains responsible for tax settings and for the fiscal documents issued.

External service

This plugin relies on the IntelliPOS service operated by Obelus d.o.o. Nothing is sent until an administrator enters an IntelliPOS instance address and credentials, tests the connection, or enables fiscalization.

  • Requests go only to the IntelliPOS instance address entered by the administrator (https).
  • Sent for authentication: the configured username and password.
  • Sent for receipts and refunds: order number and external ID, items, quantities, prices, tax labels, payment amounts, the customer’s billing e-mail address (used by IntelliPOS to deliver the receipt when receipt e-mail is enabled), and the customer’s tax ID or identifier when required.
  • Service: intellipos.rs · Privacy Policy · Terms of Use

Support

User guide (Serbian): intellipos.rs. Technical support: +381 67 750 0005, info@obelus.rs, Monday to Friday 08:00–22:00 (Belgrade time). Sales and presentations: Monday to Friday 08:00–16:00.
sections.installation:
1. Make a backup of your site and database.
  2. Upload the plugin in Plugins > Add Plugin > Upload Plugin, or install it from the directory, and activate it. WooCommerce must be active.
  3. Open WooCommerce > Settings > IntelliPOS.
  4. Enter the IntelliPOS instance address (https), username and password, save, and click “Test connection”.
  5. Enter the tax labels used by your IntelliPOS instance and map your payment methods.
  6. To test first, set “Vrsta računa” (invoice type) to “Obuka” (training). Place a few test orders, check the training receipts in IntelliPOS under Dokumenti > Obuka, then set the invoice type back to “Promet”.
  7. Fiscalize one controlled order manually (Order actions > IntelliPOS: Fiskalizuj račun), check the receipt in IntelliPOS, then enable automatic fiscalization.

Upgrading from 1.0.3: settings, receipts, refunds and order history are kept. On first run the plugin records the state of existing orders without contacting IntelliPOS; orders whose earlier outcome was unclear are marked “unknown outcome” for review.
sections.faq:
Is the plugin free? Can I fiscalize orders for free?

The plugin is free and there is no additional fee for it. Fiscalization requires an active IntelliPOS license: RSD 14,388 + VAT per year without advance invoices, or RSD 18,000 + VAT per year with advance invoices (prices as of October 2026). Without a license, the plugin cannot issue receipts.

How can I test the plugin without issuing real fiscal receipts?

Set WooCommerce > Settings > IntelliPOS > “Vrsta računa” to “Obuka” (training). Every new order then gets a training receipt (“ОВО НИЈЕ ФИСКАЛНИ РАЧУН”), which is not recorded as turnover and is shown in IntelliPOS under Dokumenti > Obuka. A warning is shown in the admin area while training mode is on. When you are done, set it back to “Promet”. Orders that received a training receipt keep it and are not sent again as Promet, so use separate test orders. Refunds work the same way in training mode and produce a training refund. Training receipts are not counted towards the receipts included in the IntelliPOS license.

My staging site is a copy of production. How do I give it its own integration ID?

On the staging site, open WooCommerce > Settings > IntelliPOS > “ID integracije”, expand “Generiši novi ID integracije”, confirm and click the button. Only the staging site gets a new ID; the production site keeps its own. Compare the ID shown on both sites: they must differ, and the production ID must be the same as before.

This also turns on test copy protection on the staging site. Orders copied from production carry real fiscal receipts, and a refund of such a receipt would be a real refund even in training mode, so the protection blocks fiscalization, refunds and receipt e-mails for every order that existed before the new ID, and allows only training receipts for new orders. The protection is based on order numbers. If you copy the production database to staging again, the new ID and the protection are overwritten: generate a new ID again.

Do I need an IntelliPOS account?

Yes. The plugin connects WooCommerce to an IntelliPOS instance with a security element; IntelliPOS issues the receipts.

When is the receipt issued?

When the order reaches the status you select in the settings (for example “Processing”), or when you run “IntelliPOS: Fiskalizuj račun” from the order actions.

What happens if IntelliPOS or the internet is unavailable?

If the request did not reach IntelliPOS, the order shows an error and nothing was issued; you can send it again from the order screen. If the request was sent but the answer did not arrive, the outcome is unknown: the plugin blocks every new attempt until an administrator checks IntelliPOS and records the result on the resolution page.

Can the same order be fiscalized twice?

The plugin sends only one request per order and blocks repeats after a confirmed receipt or an unknown outcome. Because the IntelliPOS service does not currently reject duplicate requests, a duplicate is still possible if an administrator confirms “not issued” for a receipt that actually exists. The resolution page asks for a check in IntelliPOS, a waiting period and a written reason before anything can be sent again.

Does the plugin confirm that the customer received the receipt e-mail?

No. IntelliPOS sends the e-mail. The order shows “request accepted” when IntelliPOS accepts the send request, but the plugin cannot see whether the message reached the customer’s mailbox. If a customer does not receive it, give them the receipt from IntelliPOS and contact support.

Are refunds supported?

Full refunds of a fiscal receipt are supported, manually or automatically when the WooCommerce order is fully refunded. Before a full refund the plugin checks in IntelliPOS that no part of the receipt was refunded already; if it was, or if this cannot be confirmed after earlier WooCommerce refunds, the refund goes to manual review instead of being sent. Partial refunds are sent only when “Fiskalizuj delimične povraćaje” is turned on (see below); otherwise they are recorded in the order notes.

How do partial refunds work?

Turn on “Automatska fiskalna refundacija” and “Fiskalizuj delimične povraćaje” in WooCommerce > Settings > IntelliPOS and click “Proveri podršku”. Partial refunds need a newer IntelliPOS server; the plugin checks this again for every receipt before sending and sends nothing to an older server.

Each WooCommerce refund entered by items (a whole item, part of the quantity, part of an item’s amount, shipping or fees) becomes its own fiscal refund of the original receipt. Several partial refunds per order are supported. After the first partial refund the remainder of the receipt is always refunded as a partial refund, never as a second full refund.

A refund is not sent and goes to manual review, with the reason in the order notes, when it cannot be matched to the receipt unambiguously: an amount-only refund without items, a quantity and amount that do not match the receipt price, an item that is not on the receipt or appears on it at two prices, a refund that would exceed what is left, a refund that was already issued directly in IntelliPOS, or an earlier refund of the order with an unknown outcome. On the resolution page the administrator links the refund issued in IntelliPOS, checks again and sends, or marks that the plugin does not issue it.

Is it safe to turn partial refunds off again or to go back to an older version?

Yes. After the first partial refund of an order the plugin never sends a full refund of that receipt. With the setting on, the remainder is sent as a partial refund; with the setting turned off later, nothing is sent and the order note says to refund the remainder in IntelliPOS. Going back to 1.0.7 keeps orders with partial refunds safe (their full refund goes to manual review). Going back below 1.0.7 removes the full refund safety check for other orders.

How do business customers enter their tax ID?

Checkout gets a customer type field. Business customers enter the company name and the 9-digit tax ID (PIB), which is printed on the receipt.

How are tax labels mapped?

Standard, reduced and zero-rate WooCommerce tax classes are mapped to the labels configured in the settings (for example Ђ, Е and Г). A product can override its label. When WooCommerce calculates VAT, the plugin checks that each item’s rate matches its label and does not send the receipt if it does not.

Does the plugin guarantee legal compliance?

No. It transfers order data to your IntelliPOS ESIR, which issues the fiscal documents. Settings such as tax labels and the moment of fiscalization remain the merchant’s responsibility.
sections.changelog:
1.1.1

  • Clearer administration screens for refunds; no change to fiscal logic, requests, calculations or the database.
  • When IntelliPOS could not be read before a partial refund was sent, the message now says that nothing was sent, instead of a warning that a document may already exist. The resend confirmation on the resolution page now matches the real state: a request that never reached IntelliPOS is described as such, while requests that were sent keep the strict duplicate warning.
  • The order panel shows how much of the receipt is still to be refunded fiscally, based on the fiscal documents issued or linked by the plugin, and highlights when WooCommerce has refunded more than was refunded fiscally. It is not shown while a refund is in progress or has an unknown outcome.
  • The refund list shows the IntelliPOS document number (for example 38/234ПР) and the refund amount also before a refund is issued.
  • Resolution page: page title, the refund amount instead of the order amount, the issued document instead of an old error message after success, a refund number as the example for refunds, and no instruction to re-enter an existing WooCommerce refund.

1.1.0

  • Includes the 1.0.7 full refund safety check. It is always on, whether or not partial refunds are turned on.
  • New, optional “Fiskalizuj delimične povraćaje” (fiscalize partial refunds) setting, off by default. When it is on (together with automatic fiscal refunds), each WooCommerce refund becomes its own fiscal refund through the IntelliPOS GetRefundItems and PartialRefund methods: a whole item, part of the quantity, part of an item’s amount, shipping and fees. Several partial refunds per order are supported.
  • After the first partial refund the plugin never refunds the whole receipt again: the remainder (the “IntelliPOS: Refundiraj ceo račun” action, or a refund that closes the order) is sent as PartialRefund without items. This also applies if the setting is later turned off.
  • Support is checked for every receipt before anything is sent (strict check of the GetRefundItems answer). With an older IntelliPOS server (no PartialRefund) the plugin behaves like 1.0.7.
  • Refunds that cannot be matched unambiguously (amount-only refunds, quantity and amount that do not match the receipt price, a price split on the receipt, refunds issued directly in IntelliPOS, older receipts whose items cannot be linked) are not sent; they go to “manual review” with an explanation, where an administrator can link a refund issued in IntelliPOS, re-check and send, or decide that the plugin does not issue it.
  • The plugin checks quantities and amounts itself (per item and in total, against the items actually sent on the receipt) in addition to the IntelliPOS checks, locks each order while a refund is prepared, and does not send a new refund while an earlier one has an unknown outcome.
  • New, optional “Automatska provera nepoznatog ishoda” setting (off by default): for a receipt or full refund with an unknown outcome the plugin looks the document up in IntelliPOS by its external ID (read only) and links it when exactly one matching document exists. Nothing is ever re-sent automatically. For partial refunds the check runs whenever partial refunds are on.
  • The items actually sent on each new receipt are stored with their link to the order items. For older receipts the original IntelliPOS document is the source.
  • Database: new columns in the operations table only (no existing column changes). Downgrading to 1.0.7, 1.0.6 or 1.0.5 after partial refunds were issued keeps those orders safe: a later full refund of such an order is marked “unknown” instead of being sent, and refunds in manual review stay blocked. Downgrading below 1.0.7 removes the full refund safety fix for other orders.

1.0.7

  • Safety fix for full refunds: IntelliPOS does not check earlier refunds of the same receipt, so a full refund sent after part of the receipt was already refunded (for example in the IntelliPOS portal) refunded that part a second time. Before every full refund the plugin now reads the state of the receipt in IntelliPOS (read only: GetRefundItems on newer IntelliPOS servers, and the list of refund documents that reference the receipt). The full refund is sent only when IntelliPOS confirms that nothing has been refunded yet, or, on an older IntelliPOS server without GetRefundItems, when there is no sign of an earlier refund in WooCommerce either.
  • If the order has more than one WooCommerce refund or a partial one, IntelliPOS shows an earlier refund, or the answer is unclear, the full refund is not sent and goes to “manual review” with an explanation. On the resolution page an administrator can link the refund issued in IntelliPOS, or re-check (the plugin sends only if IntelliPOS then confirms that nothing was refunded). If IntelliPOS cannot be reached for the check, nothing is sent and the refund can be started again with the “IntelliPOS: Refundiraj ceo račun” action.
  • Unchanged: a single full refund of an order with no earlier refunds is sent as before. Known limit: on an older IntelliPOS server, a partial refund issued in the IntelliPOS portal without a link to the receipt cannot be detected when WooCommerce shows no earlier refund either; check the receipt in IntelliPOS before refunding such orders.
  • No database changes. Downgrading to 1.0.6 keeps refunds that are already in manual review blocked, but removes this check for all new full refunds, so the double refund risk returns; downgrade only if necessary and check refunds in IntelliPOS before refunding.

1.0.6

  • New “Generiši novi ID integracije” (generate a new integration ID) in the IntelliPOS settings, for administrators. Use it on a staging or test copy of a store so that it no longer shares the integration ID with production.
  • Only this installation changes: nothing is sent to IntelliPOS, and credentials, invoice type, automatic fiscalization, the site address and the receipt history stay as they are. Operations already started keep their external ID.
  • Generating a new ID also turns on a local “test copy protection” on that installation: orders that already existed (typically copied from production) are no longer fiscalized, refunded or e-mailed from it, in any mode, including training; new orders can only receive training receipts and training refunds. The protection is checked when an operation starts and again immediately before the request is sent. An administrator can turn it off only after a warning and an explicit confirmation. A normal update to 1.0.6 does not turn it on.
  • Fix: the “site address changed” box in the IntelliPOS settings (“same store on a new address” / “this is a copy”) now works. Since 1.0.4 its button only saved the WooCommerce settings, because the box was rendered inside the WooCommerce settings form.

1.0.5

  • New “Invoice type” setting: Promet (fiscal receipt, default) or Obuka (training). Training receipts are not fiscal receipts and are not recorded as turnover, so the shop can be tested safely.
  • The invoice type is fixed at the first attempt for each order and never changes on a later retry. Training receipts use their own external ID.
  • Training receipts can be refunded like fiscal receipts (full refund, manually or automatically); IntelliPOS issues a training refund, which is not recorded as turnover.
  • A warning is shown in the admin area while training mode is on.
  • The resolution page points to Dokumenti > Obuka for training receipts and accepts training document numbers (for example 3/70ОП, and 2/72ОР for a training refund).

1.0.4.1

  • Important reliability and fiscal-safety update for 1.0.3 users. This is the first WordPress.org release that includes all 1.0.4 changes listed below.
  • Email status wording: an accepted SendMail request is shown as “request accepted”, not as delivered. IntelliPOS confirms only that it accepted the request.

1.0.4

  • Every fiscal operation is recorded in its own table: one fiscalization record and one refund record per order, each with a fixed external ID.
  • Requests with an unknown outcome are never resent automatically; new guided resolution page with an audit log.
  • Background fiscalization; automatic refunds wait for an unconfirmed receipt and are sent once.
  • Fees are sent as receipt items; totals, currency and VAT rates are checked before sending.
  • Payment method mapping in the settings; production tax labels (Ђ, Е, Г, А).
  • Block checkout validates the company tax ID; the sale receipt carries only a company tax ID.
  • Staging/copy protection; only administrators can change connection settings; https required.
  • Receipt time shown from the receipt (Europe/Belgrade).
  • Safe upgrade from 1.0.3 with review of unclear historical outcomes.

Earlier versions: see changelog.txt.

short_description: Issue Serbian fiscal receipts for WooCommerce orders through your IntelliPOS ESIR, automatically or manually, including full and partial refunds.
